title: Working line: the bot's mark and what it is doing now
evidence: Working line in Transcript.tsx + styles.css: row 180 ms, mark 340 ms spring, label 180 ms (+220 ms first), shimmer steps(60) 2.2 s, face squash and tilt, exit 140 ms. Starts with the mark alone, like the oracle; "Typing…" while text streams (not for text that lands within a frame). Gate B: "replied" lands with the reply bubble (0.79.3: the same ms on all 4 turns; ours 2–3 ms after, was ~103 ms, which put it after storage's Unread dot) and the exit is inside budget on 4 turns, long-answer (Grok 0.79.3) included: one reply of 1214 characters after 4.2 s of "Typing…", line gone 240 ms after it. The row comes with the bot's Working state (Barkpark's fleet stream, event: state), as the oracle's comes with its rail's Working: storage's row 0.8 s after "is working" now matches (Gate B working#1, 2016 vs 2014 ms; a row ignoring the state fails it, early by 776 ms). The rail's Working was judged as its own Gate B moment on the three 0.79.2 traces (rail:working, within 3 ms; from the turn's start it failed storage, early by 777 ms); those are superseded by the 0.79.3 re-records of 2026-11-10, which show no Working on the open bot. 0.79.3 never says Working on the open bot (long-answer), so there the line is the state's only witness: the stand-in flips it at the line (turn.ts, fromRow); the UI holding the line 300 ms longer fails working#1, late by 303 ms. Tool labels: a host with item events (task-f13fc4b4dc2af6de) sends each tool call with its name and input, and the line says it (Bash's description, else the tool). Missing: the oracle's summary labels ("Mulling it over", "Checking the storage", "Explaining ocean tides") are its own summaries of the turn: the say-hi turns call no tool, so no host event can carry them.
